subject: Urgent: EmberGate AZ routing chaos — immediate mitigation and cross-region plan
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@embergate.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@embergate.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production errors spiking in us-west-2 — request immediate response

Hi Vanessa / Markus,

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx errors and token latency for our primary deployment in us-west-2 around 08:40 PDT. Errors are hitting our checkout flow and impacting revenue — page load/response times climb from ~600ms to multiple seconds, and about 12% of requests are returning 5xx. We attached a sample log bundle (perf_logs_20270530.zip).

This looks regional — other metrics indicate queues building and a KV cache pressure pattern. Can Redwood initiate an immediate mitigation (cross-region redirect or canary routing) while you triage root cause? We need visibility on expected failover time and whether you'll take a temporary traffic redirect to us-east-1 or eu-west-1.

Elena
Head of Platform, EmberGate

Attachments: perf_logs_20270530.zip (log bundle, 12MB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production errors spiking in us-west-2 — EmberGate

Markus / Marissa — forwarding EmberGate. They report a 12% 5xx rate and significant latency. They attached logs. Can SRE/ops confirm current queue depth, KV hit ratio, and whether the us-west-2 pool is degraded or overloaded? If this looks like AZ-level routing/egress issues, we should prepare a controlled cross-region canary redirect (10%) to us-east-1, with alert thresholds and rollback.

Log link: https://drive.redwood.com/embergate/incident/1184
HubSpot: HS-1184

Vanessa
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

> We started seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx errors and token latency...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, SRE Oncall <sre-oncall@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors spiking in us-west-2 — EmberGate

+ quick triage notes:
- Telemetry: queue depth on us-west-2 service pool at 09:30 is +320% vs baseline; KV cache local hit rate dropped ~18% at 08:42. No clear model degradation — bottleneck looks infra (egress latency + spot preemption? further analysis ongoing).
- Recommended immediate mitigation: staged cross-region canary to us-east-1 at 10% traffic (sticky sessions respected) for 30 minutes while we monitor latency and error rate. If stable, ramp to 50% over 30 minutes.
- Operational runway: we can spin dedicated extra instances in us-east-1 under Dedicated buffer (15–20% cost hit).
- Risks: cold cache miss rate will spike initially; token/seq consistency OK due to session affinity.

I prepared a minimal operational MOP (MOP_reroute_v1.pdf) and cost estimate (cost_estimate_embergate.csv). Need sign-off from Markus for cross-region cost and from Hannah for exec escalation/credit ask (they are a premium strategic customer).

Marissa
Customer Reliability Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MOP_reroute_v1.pdf, cost_estimate_embergate.csv

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EmberGate — approve canary and quick credit authority

Hannah — we need your quick authorization to proceed with the canary redirect and to approve a one-time credit if the failover window results in measurable customer impact. EmberGate is flagged as strategic (DG-1184).

Details:
- Proposed action: 10% traffic reroute to us-east-1 immediately, 30m observation. If errors drop <1% and latency median drops below 450ms, continue ramp at operator discretion.
- Estimated incremental cost: ~$7k for the first hour (see cost_estimate_embergate.csv).
- Customer ask: they want a formal ETA and a short summary for execs (Elena will escalate internally).

Please confirm within 15 minutes so Marissa/SRE can execute. If you prefer, mark approval for credit as up to 15% of the hourly charge (we can do a bounded approval now).

Markus Klein
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EmberGate — approve canary and quick credit authority

Markus / team — approved. Proceed with 10% canary to us-east-1 now. Authorize up to 15% one-time credit if we observe customer-facing errors >5% for more than 20 minutes during the mitigation window. Keep logs and timeline for postmortem and credit calc.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@embergate.com>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@embergate.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors spiking in us-west-2 — Redwood mitigation plan

Elena — quick update:
- We are initiating a staged canary redirect of 10% traffic to us-east-1 at 10:30 PDT, monitoring key metrics (5xx rate, p95 latency, token errors).
- Expected window to see improvement: 10–20 minutes after canary steady state.
- We will hold for 30 minutes, then decide ramp/rollback.
- We've authorized a one-time credit threshold for sustained >5% customer errors during mitigation.

Marissa & SRE are executing now; I've attached the operator runbook. Will follow up with a short exec summary once we have first metric delta.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MOP_reroute_v1.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@embergate.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-mitigation update: EmberGate us-west-2 canary results and next steps

Elena / Sam — final update for today:

Summary:
- Action taken: Staged 10% traffic canary to us-east-1 at 10:30 PDT, observed for 30 minutes.
- Observed impact: 5xx rate on routed traffic dropped from 12% -> 0.9% within 12 minutes; median latency improved from ~1.2s -> 380ms on canary.
- Ramp: after successful canary, we ramped to 50% by 11:20 PDT. Error rate stabilized <1% overall and queues returned to baseline by 11:45 PDT.
- Costs & credits: incremental cost for the mitigation window ~ $6.2k; per Hannah approval, a one-time credit of 10% was applied to the May invoice as goodwill.

Next steps:
- Root cause: SRE is continuing analysis; early signal points to an egress layer behind us-west-2 AZ B network appliances (vendor-level deg). We will provide a full postmortem (timeline + remediation + compensating controls) by EOD tomorrow.
- Action items for EmberGate: we recommend a short traffic pin to us-east-1 for scheduled batch windows next week while we verify router flaps are fully resolved.

Thanks for the quick coordination — we prioritized EmberGate as a strategic account for rapid remediation.

Markus Klein
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-drafts (placeholder), cost_estimate_embergate.csv
